propositions: The enrich-drain advisory lock is held across NO-TIMEOUT LLM calls (437s–131s observed), creating single-flight bottleneck where every spawned drain child exits with lock-held skip, producing a 1,046-entry backlog.

The restructure splits drain() into three phases: COLLECT (under lock, <3s with concurrency guard), ENRICH (lock-free LLM calls), and FINALIZE (revalidate content-hash snapshot; stale entries skip emit and re-enqueue with soak 0).
Batch cap is raised from 5 to 20 and dynamically clamped to lease_ttl_s // 40 (~22 at 15-min default lease) to prevent per-run batch outrunning its lease mid-run.
Lock-not-held-across-LLM mechanism is pinned by an instrumented-runner test that acquires the drain lock from inside every run() call, proving the lock is released before enrich.

Concurrent drainers are bounded by a guard capping 3 distinct live-lease drainer_ids; a 4th drain returns {"skipped": "concurrency-cap"}, and stale-at-writeback entries are re-enqueued with soak 0 (counted as stale_skipped).

Pre-change ceiling: 5 items per multi-minute exclusive lock hold; post-change: up to 3 concurrent drainers × ~20 items per batch with lock held only during collect (~1.5–2.9s), delivering 9× per-item lock reduction and eliminating hung-provider-wedges-every-drainer failure class.
